podcast.body: A successful track from "The Man-Machine," it is listed as one of the dance-pop songs that solidified Kraftwerk's impact on popular music. Its cold, precise yet deeply physical sound, combined with repetitive patterns and simple melodies, made it highly memorable and bailable. "funcionó nindos del Dance Pop como Translíope Express, showroom dumis, de model, de robots, Crafwerke había logrado lo que muchas artistas llevaban años señando."

podcast.body: Released in 1978, this song was part of Kraftwerk's work that garnered international attention, helping to popularize electronic sounds. Its release followed about five years of the band's experimentation with synthesizer technology, contributing to their reputation and influencing subsequent artists with its distinct, somewhat cold and artificial aesthetic. "This is from 1978. She's a modern and she's looking good. I'd like to take a home that's on the stove."
